texts.preamble: Raj Veer Singh vs State Of U.P. on 24 September, 2019 Author: Siddharth Bench: Siddharth
texts.facts: Offence under sections 60(2) of Excise Act is bailable and trible by Magistrate. False recovery has been alleged.
texts.arguments: Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State. Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been enacted by the legislature and hence the implication of the applicant under sections 272 I.P.C is unjustified. On the other hand learned AGA has opposed the prayer for bail. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence on record regarding complicity of the accused, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties noted herein above, larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Dataram Singh Vs. State of U.P. and another reported in (2018)3 SCC 22 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of Raj Veer Singh vs State Of U.P. on 24 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78477202/ 1 the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
